result:
The test suite is clean and all 46 tests pass. I wrote `StringUtilsAgentTest` covering `StringUtils`' major method families — empty/blank checks, case/alpha/numeric predicates, trim/strip, equals/compare, contains/indexOf/lastIndexOf/ordinalIndexOf, substring variants, padding/centering, capitalize/swapCase, chomp/chop/reverse/rotate/repeat, replace/remove families, abbreviate/truncate, wrap/unwrap, split variants, join variants, startsWith/endsWith, default-value helpers, normalizeSpace/deleteWhitespace, difference/common prefix, Levenshtein/Jaro-Winkler/fuzzy distance, overlay, code points, and case conversion — with boundary cases (null, empty, negative/overflow indices, illegal widths) drawn from the class's own documented examples, and corrected several of my own initial expectation mistakes (e.g. `chomp("foo","foo")`, `replaceOnce` semantics, `stripStart` trailing chars, `containsAny` case-sensitivity, `indexOfAny` index) by cross-checking the Javadoc.

No bugs in `StringUtils` were found — every assertion that initially failed was due to a wrong expectation on my part, and after fixing those expectations to match the documented/actual behavior, all 46 tests pass.
